title: Validate adaptive TPS and backpressure probes for private edge workers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Design, implement and validate a set of lightweight probes for private (VPC) edge workers that measure tokens-per-second (TPS), node backpressure (saturation), request latency quantiles, and error rates with low cardinality and minimal performance impact. These probes must be deployable via existing Terraform IaC modules, exportable to our Prometheus / OTLP pipeline, and consumable by the SLO aggregation job used by the Console.

Scope:
- Instrument edge worker runtime to emit aggregated TPS and queue/backpressure indicators at 1s and 10s granularities.
- Add latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) and request error counters (4xx/5xx categorizations) with fixed low-cardinality labels (node_id, region, model_family).
- Provide Terraform module inputs and templates to enable probe sidecars or exporter config in Private deployments.
- Validate probe stability under high load and during upgrade/rolling restart scenarios.
- Define Alerting rules and SLOs (target examples: latency p95 < 120ms, error rate < 0.5%, sustained TPS saturation alert when available_capacity < 10% for > 2m).

Non-goals: per-request tracing or high-cardinality per-customer counters (handled by separate billing observability), full rollout automation to Dedicated clusters (out of scope for this ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Probe metrics available from default Private Terraform deploy (example terraform module input: enable_edge_probes = true).
Prometheus/OTLP pipeline receives TPS, backpressure, latency, and error metrics with <5% overhead on CPU during 95th percentile load test.
Dashboards in Grafana show p50/p95/p99 latency, TPS, and available_capacity per-region and per-node for last 24h.
SLO aggregation job consumes new metrics and computes rollup SLOs; example SLO alert fires in staging when we inject artificial backpressure.
Runbook added and linked in Confluence with playbook steps for triage and rollback when probes cause high cardinality or cost spikes.

comments: 2026-02-11 Aisha Patel: Kickoff doc created in Confluence — architecture options compared: sidecar exporter vs in-process metrics. Decided to prototype sidecar first to minimize runtime surface changes.

2026-02-16 Marco Nguyen: Prototype sidecar emits aggregated TPS using fixed 5-second buckets. Early load test shows 1.8% CPU overhead at 2k rps — within acceptable range. Instrumentation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/5521

2026-02-21 Erin Cole: Reviewed metric schema. Feedback: reduce label cardinality by replacing request.path with model_family only; add a 'saturation_reason' label with limited values (queue_length, cpu_pressure, kv_lock).

2026-02-25 Luis Ortega: Load test in staging (10k rps) with synthetic tokens-per-request distribution completed. Observed metric cardinality spike due to ephemeral session_id label — patched exporter to drop session_id. Re-ran test; spike eliminated.

2026-03-01 Priya Shah: Draft alerting rules submitted. Proposed: alert when available_capacity < 10% for 2m OR sustained p95 latency > 300ms for 5m. Requested adding a delay window to avoid flapping during autoscaler bursts.
2026-03-03 Security Team: Quick review — confirmed no PII emitted; recommend TLS between exporter and collector for Private installs. Added to Terraform module variables.

2026-03-05 Marco Nguyen: Validation in staging shows SLO aggregation job picks up new metrics and dashboard displays expected curves. Next: run canary on one customer VPC and monitor for 48h before broader rollout.
notes: Decision: Use sidecar exporter + OTLP in PRIVATE installs to keep main runtime unchanged; this reduces risk during rolling upgrades.

Trade-off: Aggregating TPS at 1s windows yields faster detection but increases metric emission rate; chose dual-window approach (1s for immediate alerts internal, 10s for SLO rollups) to balance cost.
Open question: Should we expose per-tenant TPS as an opt-in feature? Proposal: opt-in via terraform var with warning about cardinality/cost.
